qranalytics.title: QR Code Analytics — Track Every Scan | ScanFence
qranalytics.description: QR code analytics that log every scan: location, device, hour, and outcome. Real-time campaign tracking and attribution for dynamic QR codes. EU-hosted, cookieless, SOC-2.
qranalytics.hero.lede: Turn a printed square into a live data stream. ScanFence logs every scan — where it happened, on what device, at what hour, and whether it routed or got blocked. QR analytics with no cookies, no app, and no reprinting.
qranalytics.records.lede: Four fields land the instant a camera meets your code. No tag manager, no cookie banner, no SDK — the redirect itself is the measurement.
qranalytics.records.field1.label: Time
qranalytics.records.field1.body: An exact timestamp for every scan, down to the second — so you can read demand by hour, not just by day.
qranalytics.records.field2.label: Location
qranalytics.records.field2.body: City and geofence for each scan. See which venue, which perimeter, and which region drove the traffic.
qranalytics.records.field3.label: Device
qranalytics.records.field3.body: Operating system and browser — iOS · Safari, Android · Chrome — captured without a single cookie.
qranalytics.records.field4.label: Outcome
qranalytics.records.field4.body: Routed or blocked, and why: outside the fence, out of the window, or clean through to the destination.
qranalytics.campaign.lede: Give every poster, table tent, and flyer its own dynamic code and read them side by side. QR campaign tracking that tells you what worked, where, and when — without UTM guesswork.
qranalytics.campaign.point1.title: Per-code, per-campaign
qranalytics.campaign.point1.body: Break scans down by individual code or roll them up by campaign. Compare the Tuesday flyer against the window decal in one view.
qranalytics.campaign.point2.title: Geographic + time attribution
qranalytics.campaign.point2.body: See which city and which hour a campaign landed. Pair geofencing with time-based routing to prove exactly where and when demand happened.
qranalytics.campaign.point3.title: Blocked-scan insight
qranalytics.campaign.point3.body: Scans outside the fence or off-schedule are logged, not lost — and they never count against your quota. Missed intent becomes data.
qranalytics.beyond.heading: Most QR generators stop at the redirect.
qranalytics.beyond.lede: A static QR code points somewhere and goes quiet. ScanFence keeps reading — the routing engine is the analytics layer.
qranalytics.beyond.item1.title: Cookieless by design
qranalytics.beyond.item1.body: Scan data comes from the redirect, not a tracker. No consent banner to bolt on, no third-party pixel.
qranalytics.beyond.item2.title: EU-hosted, SOC-2 Type II
qranalytics.beyond.item2.body: Scan metadata stays in the EU (Ireland region) and never leaves it. Privacy is the default, not a setting.
qranalytics.beyond.item3.title: Routing is the metric
qranalytics.beyond.item3.body: Because the code is dynamic, every resolution is measured. Change the destination and the analytics follow the code, not the print run.
qranalytics.beyond.item4.title: Real-time receipts
qranalytics.beyond.item4.body: Read scans as they land, at sub-120ms median routing. No overnight batch, no waiting for a report.
qranalytics.faq.heading: QR analytics, answered.
qranalytics.faq.q1: Can I track QR code scans by location?
qranalytics.faq.a1: Yes. Every scan records the city it came from and which geofence it fell inside, so you can see exactly where your codes are being used — by venue, perimeter, or region.
qranalytics.faq.q2: What data does ScanFence capture on each scan?
qranalytics.faq.a2: Four fields per scan: the exact time, the location, the device (OS and browser), and the outcome — routed or blocked, with the reason. No personal data, no cookies.
qranalytics.faq.q3: Do blocked scans count toward my quota?
qranalytics.faq.a3: No. Scans blocked for being outside a geofence or off-schedule are logged for your analytics but never count against your monthly scan quota.
qranalytics.faq.q4: Is QR code analytics with ScanFence GDPR-friendly?
qranalytics.faq.a4: Yes. Analytics come from the redirect itself — no cookies, no cross-site tracking — and all scan metadata is hosted in the EU (Ireland) under SOC-2 Type II. It never leaves the EU.
qranalytics.faq.q5: Can I track multiple QR codes as one campaign?
qranalytics.faq.a5: Yes. Give each asset its own dynamic code and compare them individually, or roll them up by campaign for clean attribution across posters, tables, and flyers.
qranalytics.faq.q6: Do I have to reprint a code to change where it points?
qranalytics.faq.a6: Never. Codes are dynamic — repoint the destination anytime and it lands instantly. Your analytics stay attached to the same printed code across every change.

qrrestaurants.title: QR Codes for Restaurants — Menus That Route Themselves | ScanFence
qrrestaurants.description: QR codes for restaurants that serve the right menu by language, location, and time of day — from one printed code. A restaurant scan app without the app, with analytics on every scan.
qrrestaurants.hero.lede: Print the code once and let it read the room. ScanFence routes each scan to the right menu — by language, by location, by the hour — and logs every one. No app for your guests to download. No reprint when the menu changes.
qrrestaurants.uses.lede: The same square on every table can behave differently for every guest — because the routing happens after the scan, not on the paper.
qrrestaurants.uses.case1.title: The right language, automatically
qrrestaurants.uses.case1.body: A scan in the tourist quarter opens the English menu; the same code across town opens the local one. Geofencing picks the language so your guests don't have to.
qrrestaurants.uses.case2.title: Breakfast, lunch, dinner — on a clock
qrrestaurants.uses.case2.body: Time-based routing swaps the menu as the day turns. Brunch until 11:00, lunch after, the cocktail list at night — one code, no restickering.
qrrestaurants.uses.case3.title: One code per table or per venue
qrrestaurants.uses.case3.body: Run a code per table, per location, or per campaign and read each one separately. Built for chains and multi-site operators.
qrrestaurants.app.lede: Your guests already have the only app they need — the camera. Point, tap, menu. Nothing to install, nothing to sign into.
qrrestaurants.app.point1.title: Zero friction for guests
qrrestaurants.app.point1.body: No store download, no account, no wait. The menu opens in the browser the instant the camera reads the code.
qrrestaurants.app.point2.title: Change it at 11:47, it lands at 11:47
qrrestaurants.app.point2.body: Sold out of the special? Repoint the menu and the update is live immediately — on every table, without touching a printer.
qrrestaurants.app.point3.title: Every scan on the receipt
qrrestaurants.app.point3.body: See how many guests scanned, from where, and when — turning a paper menu into measurable footfall.
qrrestaurants.integrate.heading: Integrate QR into your restaurant in an afternoon.
qrrestaurants.integrate.lede: No POS project, no developer. Point a dynamic code at the menu you already have online.
qrrestaurants.integrate.step1.title: Create the code
qrrestaurants.integrate.step1.body: Generate one dynamic QR code for the venue. Print it on table tents, windows, and receipts.
qrrestaurants.integrate.step2.title: Point it at your menu
qrrestaurants.integrate.step2.body: Link it to your existing online menu, PDF, or ordering page — and swap the destination anytime without reprinting.
qrrestaurants.integrate.step3.title: Add the rules
qrrestaurants.integrate.step3.body: Draw a geofence and set the hours. Decide which menu each scan opens, by place and by time.
qrrestaurants.integrate.step4.title: Read the scans
qrrestaurants.integrate.step4.body: Watch the receipt fill in — per table, per location, per hour — and adjust the routing as you learn.
qrrestaurants.pricing.heading: Starts at $4.99 a month.
qrrestaurants.pricing.body: The Basic plan covers one venue, one menu, one operator — 100 dynamic codes, 25,000 scans a month, EU-hosted. Add locations and seats as you grow.
qrrestaurants.faq.heading: Restaurant QR codes, answered.
qrrestaurants.faq.q1: How do QR code menus work for restaurants?
qrrestaurants.faq.a1: Print one dynamic QR code and point it at your online menu. Guests scan with their phone camera and the menu opens in the browser — no app required. You can change where the code points anytime without reprinting.
qrrestaurants.faq.q2: Do my guests need to download an app to scan the menu?
qrrestaurants.faq.a2: No. The phone's built-in camera reads the code and opens the menu in the browser. There is nothing for guests to install or sign into — it works like a restaurant scan app without the app.
qrrestaurants.faq.q3: Can one QR code show different menus at different times of day?
qrrestaurants.faq.a3: Yes. Time-based routing lets a single code open the breakfast menu in the morning and the dinner or cocktail menu at night — automatically, on the schedule you set.
qrrestaurants.faq.q4: Can the same code show menus in different languages?
qrrestaurants.faq.a4: Yes. With GPS geofencing the code can open the right language for the location — an English menu in a tourist area and the local language elsewhere — from the one printed code.
qrrestaurants.faq.q5: Can I update the menu without reprinting the QR code?
qrrestaurants.faq.a5: Always. Codes are dynamic, so you repoint them to a new menu or destination in seconds and the change is live immediately — the printed code never has to change.
qrrestaurants.faq.q6: Can I track how many people scan my restaurant's QR code?
qrrestaurants.faq.a6: Yes. Every scan is logged with its time, location, and device, so you can see footfall by table, by venue, and by hour. See QR code analytics for the full picture.
